{{Short description|Topological space in mathematics}}
In [[topology]], the '''Tychonoff plank''' is a [[topological space]] defined using [[ordinal space]]s that is a [[counterexample]] to several plausible-sounding [[conjecture]]s. It is defined as the [[topological product]] of the two [[ordinal space]]s <math>[0,\omega_1]</math> and <math>[0,\omega]</math>, where <math>\omega</math> is the [[first infinite ordinal]] and <math>\omega_1</math> the [[first uncountable ordinal]]. The '''deleted Tychonoff plank''' is obtained by deleting the point <math>\infty = (\omega_1,\omega)</math>.<ref>{{MathWorld |id=TychonoffPlank |title=Tychonoff Plank |access-date= 20 July 2025}}</ref>

==Definition==
Let <math> \Omega </math> be the set of [[ordinal number|ordinals]] which are less than or equal to <math> \omega </math> and <math> \Omega_1 </math> the set of ordinals less than or equal to <math> \omega_1 </math>. The ''Tychonoff plank'' is defined as the set <math> \Omega \times \Omega_1 </math> with the [[product topology]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Steen |first=Lynn Arthur |author-link=Lynn Arthur Steen |title=[[Counterexamples in Topology]] |last2=Seebach |first2=J. Arthur Jr. |author-link2=J. Arthur Seebach, Jr. |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |year=1995 |isbn=978-0-486-68735-3 |edition=[[Dover Publications|Dover]] reprint of 1978 |location=Berlin, New York |mr=507446 |orig-year=1978}}</ref>

The ''deleted Tychonoff plank'' is the subset <math> S = \Omega \times \Omega_1 \setminus \{ (\omega,\omega_1) \} </math>, where <math> S </math> is the plank with a corner removed.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kelley |first=John L. |author-link=John L. Kelley |title=General Topology |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |year=1975 |isbn=978-0-387-90125-1 |edition=1 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=27 |location=New York |at=Ch. 4 Ex. F |mr=370454}}</ref>

==Properties==
The Tychonoff plank is a [[compact Hausdorff space]] and is therefore a [[normal space]]. However, the deleted Tychonoff plank is non-normal.{{sfn|Steen|Seebach|1995|loc=Example 86, item 2}}  Therefore the Tychonoff plank is not [[completely normal]]. This shows that a subspace of a normal space need not be normal.  The Tychonoff plank is not [[Perfectly normal space|perfectly normal]] because it is not a [[Gδ space|G<sub>δ</sub> space]]: the singleton <math>\{\infty\}</math> is closed but not a [[Gδ set|G<sub>δ</sub> set]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Willard |first=Stephen |url=https://archive.org/details/generaltopology00will_0/page/17 |title=General Topology |publisher=[[Addison-Wesley]] |year=1970 |isbn=9780201087079 |at=[https://archive.org/details/generaltopology00will_0/page/17 17.12] |mr=264581 |url-access=registration}}</ref>

The [[Stone–Čech compactification]] of the deleted Tychonoff plank is the Tychonoff plank.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zhP2CAAAQBAJ&pg=PA95|title=The Stone-Čech Compactification|last=Walker|first=R. C.|publisher=Springer|year=1974|isbn=978-3-642-61935-9|pages=95–97|language=en}}</ref>
